content_preview.title: Home Assistant 2026.8 Drops the :8123 Port Requirement and Strips 'Advanced' Labels in Push for Approachability
content_preview.summary: Home Assistant's August release removes the long-standing :8123 port requirement for new installs and strips 'advanced' and 'expert' wording from roughly 43 places in the app.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Open Home Foundation released [Home Assistant 2026.8](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2026/08/05/release-20268/) on August 5, 2026, under the theme "Approachable by design," removing the long-standing requirement to append `:8123` to the address when reaching new installations and stripping "advanced" and "expert" labeling from dozens of places across the open-source home automation platform.

recommendations: Add home-assistant.io to config/source_allowlist.txt as an official-source domain (the project's own blog and changelog) so future Home Assistant coverage doesn't re-trigger this warning.

Consider tightening the 'system-prompt-reference' suspicious_patterns regex so it doesn't fire on ordinary product-documentation text that happens to contain the literal field name 'extra_system_prompt' or similar API parameter names.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean 651-word News piece using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Every specific — the release date, the port-requirement removal, the '43 places' figure, the Ashley/Frenck/Bram byline, the Developer Tools rename, the entity ID change, the device/config-entry change, the 40% template performance figure, the new integrations list, the battery-property deprecations, and the 2026.8.1 patch date — is attributed inline to one of the two cited sources. The 'What We Don't Know' section correctly notes the release notes don't specify a replacement port number or a single total-integration-count figure, rather than inventing either.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources read from the gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-08/home-assistant-20268-drops-the-8123-port-requirement-and-strips-advanced-labels-in-push-for-approachability/ and sha256-verified against manifest.json (both hashes matched exactly: source-0 209bbf5a...8af, source-1 0c10b73e...068). (1) source-0.html.gz — home-assistant.io/blog/2026/08/05/release-20268/, the official Home Assistant 2026.8 'Approachable by design' release-notes blog post. Confirmed verbatim: the Ashley Abbott byline and exact quote 'the Technical Program Manager at the Open Home Foundation. With Frenck taking a well-deserved break, Bram and I are teaming up to handle things this time around'; the :8123 removal section ('For years, reaching Home Assistant meant remembering to add :8123 to the address... This release starts to put that right'); the 'around 43 places' wording-removal figure; the Developer Tools → Tools rename; the Home Assistant Cloud redesign credit '@klejejs'; the entity-ID renaming feature; the device/config-entry-and-subentry change including the underlying mechanism (devices merged across integrations previously clashed on model/serial fields, now separated automatically — found in the 'A cleaner way to handle your devices' section, correctly paraphrased and not put in quote marks in the article); the '40% faster' template performance claim; every one of the 15 new integrations named in the article (Dyson Infrared, Google Health, LiteLLM, llama.cpp, Midea, NeoPool, Lyngdorf, Gatus, GeoSphere Austria Warnings, Karakeep, Harbor Sleep, Harman Luxury Audio, Fuelprices.dk, LED Infrared, ScorpionTrack all present); and the 2026.8.1 / August 7 patch date. (2) source-1.html.gz — home-assistant.io/changelogs/core-2026.8/, the full Core 2026.8 changelog. Confirmed each of the seven individually-quoted battery-property-removal changelog entries verbatim ('Remove battery prop from template vacuum', 'Remove deprecated battery level prop from Neato vacuum', 'Remove previously deprecated battery props from Romy/tplink/xiaomi_miio/Sharkiq', 'Remove previously deprecated battery prop from LG thinq') plus 'Remove deprecated classes from Service'. No hallucinated quotes or misattributed specifics found in either source — every direct quote is verbatim and every specific traces to the outlet it's attributed to.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No unsourced or fabricated claims. Headline, summary, and lead are all backed by the cited sources (confirmed above). No orphan source URLs — both cited URLs are the only two the body links to.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no editorializing or sensational language. Direct quotes are clearly marked and attributed; paraphrased material (e.g. the device-merging mechanism) is correctly left outside quote marks.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ (grep -rli 'home assistant') — no prior Home Assistant coverage found anywhere in the archive. Genuinely new topic, no duplicate or overlap with recently published stories.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns: manifest.json flagged both sources with pattern 'system-prompt-reference', excerpt: 'reads it out using text-to-speech.","start_media_id":"A media ID to start with instead of using text-to-speech.","extra_system_prompt":"Background information about the request, passed to the conversation agent. This helps the agent understand a short r'. Opened this exact text in both decompressed snapshots (identical single occurrence in each, confirmed via grep -oc). It sits inside a large embedded JSON blob documenting Home Assistant's own service/action registry (site-wide search-index data present on every home-assistant.io page), specifically the real 'assist_satellite.start_conversation' action. The full surrounding text reads: '"extra_system_prompt":"Background information about the request, passed to the conversation agent. This helps the agent understand a short reply like yes or no."' — this is product documentation describing a genuine, publicly-documented Home Assistant API parameter (passing background context to its own voice Assist conversation agent), not text addressed to an AI agent reviewing this page and not an instruction to ignore anything or withhold anything from the user. Determined to be a false positive and overridden; no claim in the article relies on or is affected by this text in any way (the article never mentions Assist, extra_system_prompt, or the actions API).
editor_notes.human_requested: human_requested is false for this submission; standard-scrutiny review applied.
recommendations: Add home-assistant.io to config/source_allowlist.txt as an official-source domain, analogous to other project blogs already allowlisted.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, accurately sourced submission. Both automated REJECT triggers were false positives on inspection — an allowlist gap on the subject's own official sources, and a coarse regex match on the site's own embedded API documentation rather than any attempt to manipulate the reviewing agent. Approved outright.
